title: Golden calf: Israel meant Jehovah under a bovine symbol—plural Elohim with singular sense; not literal bovine deity
source_text: XXVIII. Crimen istud fuit Israelitarum, quum vitulum aureum in deserto fuderunt. Mens enim ipsorum erat in figura ista exprimere, & colere Jehovam Deum Patrum suorum, qui eos de terra Aegypti eduxerat: forte quia viderant in Aegypto summum numen sub bovis symbolo coli & adorari. Id testantur ipsi, vitulo conflato, exclamantes, Ecce Deus tuus Israel, qui te eduxit de terra Aegypti. Quanquam enim in textu hebraeo sint verba pluralis numeri, sensum tamen habent singularem, cum de unico vitulo dicantur, & in scriptura satis usitatum sit, etiam quum de vero Deo sermo est, vocem Elohim, quae Deum significat, verbo pluralis numeri jungere. Ut quum Abraham dicit, Gen. 20. v. 13. Postquam errare fecerunt me Elohim de Domo Patris mei. Quod vulgata recte vertit numero singulari Postquam eduxit me Deus. Et similiter quum David Deum sic alloquitur, Quae est autem gens ut populus tuus Israel, in terra, propter quam iverunt Elohim, ut redimeret eam sibi in populum, id est, propter quam ivit Deus, ut habet etiam vulgata, Sam. 2. 7. v. 23. Quum vero de vitulo dicunt, illum esse Deum qui ipsos eduxit e terra Aegypti, proculdubio non aliud sibi volunt, quam vitulum istum illius fuisse figuram, & visibile signum: prout nihil usitatius est, quam imaginem vocare nomine rei quam illa repraesentat. Nec enim puto quemquam, qui rem attente consideraverit, sibi persuadere posse populum tam numerosum, uno quasi instanti, in eam insaniam incidere potuisse, ut crederet vitulum, quem recenter ex propriis monilibus fabricaverant, non tantum in signo & repraesentatione, sed revera & proprio sensu, esse illum ipsum Deum, qui priusquam de vitulo conflando cogitarent, tanta & tam miranda, ipsis inspectantibus, & in eorum liberationem, opera ediderat.
pass_a_gloss: That crime was of the Israelites, when they cast the golden calf in the desert. For their mind was in that figure to express, and to cultivate, Jehovah the God of their Fathers, who had led them out of the land of Egypt: perhaps because they had seen in Egypt the highest divinity cultivated and adored under the symbol of a bull. They themselves testify to that, when the calf was cast, crying out, Behold thy God, O Israel, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt. For although in the Hebrew text the words are of the plural number, yet they have a singular sense, since they are said of a single calf, and it is sufficiently usual in Scripture, even when speech is of the true God, to join the word Elohim, which signifies God, to a verb of the plural number. As when Abraham says, Gen. 20. v. 13. After the Elohim caused me to wander from the House of my Father. Which the Vulgate rightly turns in the singular number After God led me out. And likewise when David thus addresses God, And what nation is like thy people Israel, upon earth, on account of which the Elohim went, that he might redeem it for himself for a people, that is, on account of which God went, as the Vulgate also has, 2 Sam. 7. v. 23. But when they say of the calf, that it is the God who led them out of the land of Egypt, without doubt they mean nothing else, than that that calf was his figure, and visible sign: just as nothing is more usual than to call an image by the name of the thing which it represents. For I do not think that anyone who has attentively considered the matter can persuade himself that a people so numerous, in one quasi-instant, could have fallen into that madness, that they believed the calf, which they had recently fabricated from their own necklaces, not only in sign and representation, but in very deed and proper sense, to be that very God who, before they thought of casting a calf, had performed so great and so marvelous works, with themselves looking on, and for their liberation.
pass_b_english: The calf was Egypt-style bovine symbolism aimed at Jehovah, not a sudden belief that jewelry had become God.
Plural Elohim with singular force is ordinary Hebrew—even of the true God (Gen 20.13; 2 Sam 7.23).
Calling the image by the prototype’s name is stock; absolute bovine deity is psychologically incredible.

choices.why: Calf as figure of Jehovah, not Jehovah himself.
